text:
Mark Scheifele now stands alone as the Winnipeg Jets' all-time points leader, and he got there in style: four points and a shootout goal in Chicago as the Jets came back from four goals down to win 5-4. It's also part of a run. He has a six-game point streak (five goals, nine assists), and the Jets have won all six after losing the four before it.

At 33, he's still the man who makes the Jets' offense go. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 11.8 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 99th percentile among forwards, and 12 of his 26 points this season have come on the power play. His last ten games brought 18 points against 12.2 expected, so the streak has some heat in it, though his own goal scoring is, if anything, a little under his chances. The long-running catch is the other end: Evolving-Hockey had opponents creating more with him on the ice than with almost any other forward, bottom 3% in that measure. The offense has always paid for it, and so far this season it still does.
